bums me out when I see modern lesbians pluck some down and out dyke’s writing from decades ago out of its original context and hold it to task for not describing all of butch/femme/womanhood/lesbianism in totality, it always feels like these people have no idea how unlikely it was that this shred of experience would even make its way through time to them, much less actually get written down. she worked night shifts in a box factory you dorks, when she describes

other

 people she met thought of as butch either. it’s almost as if butch is a constantly shifting zone of encounter that dykes use as technology to endure the unendurable and pinning it down into one solid definition is busywork for fools.

During their institutionalization, patients must believe (or appear to believe) that the hospital is a helpful place in order to be considered “well” by the staff. 

To be discharged, a patient must confirm the psychiatric version of reality, including an acknowledgement that the hospitalization has been necessary and beneficial.

 Patients who maintain that the hospital is a prison and express this opinion to staff do not get discharged, as sociologist Robert Perrucci found when he studied discharge procedures. In one of the discharge interviews he observed, the patient gave a series of “appropriate” answers to staff questions, until the doctor asked her if she thought she had been helped. 

Patient: No, I don’t. 

Doctor: What kind of treatment have you had?

Patient: Lobotomy and shock. 

Doctor: Do you think it’s helped you or tortured you?

Patient: I think it’s tortured me. 

The interview continued, with the patient presenting a reasonable explanation of why she preferred to leave the hospital and get a laboratory job rather than take a work-release placement while remaining a patient. 

Patient: I’d do much better if the hospital would free me.

There are times when a kid is deeply upset about something an adult would consider trivial because they are very new and it’s the worst thing that’s ever happened to them. Like falling and bruising yourself when you are 3. Like the first fight with a close friend.

And sometimes it’s because their world is small and deliberately constrained! If you were getting bullied at work every day, you would start looking for a different job. If you couldn’t immediately find one, you’d still have the option of going anywhere you wanted after work to seek support or a different social circle. You hopefully know SOMEone outside of that particular job.

author: Unknown
title: I feel like folks expressing bafflement at younger readers approaching prose fiction by skipping…
content:
I feel like folks expressing bafflement at younger readers approaching prose fiction by skipping everything except the dialogue are acting like this is a problem that came out of nowhere and not the inevitable consequence of people’s formative media experiences being YouTube videos with 45 seconds of real content in a twelve-minute running time.

Like, this isn’t an unwillingness to develop media literacy; it’s what media literacy looks like when one of the basic skills for understanding the media you most frequently engage with is correctly distinguishing the bits that actually have something to say amid a sea of vacuous algorithm-chasing.

You need to understand that you are trying to tell members of the “but first I’d like to give a few shoutouts” generation that the front matter is required reading.

I think it’s really going to help to actually stop and think about: 

what is the point of acquiring social skills? 

like. is there a point beyond base level survival 

do people have useful and interesting qualities apart from what they make possible for you 

could acquiring social skills have a purpose beyond getting what you need from them to live 

can different sets of social skills work against each other? 

like say you were conditioned to prioritize certain social groups over others and make the environment inhospitable for the least valued and wanted, so you have a lot of skills for pressuring and triangulating and devaluing and dogpiling and are really good at identifying the weakest link and making them leave. 

would that work against other social skills that prioritize access and dignity and quality for stigmatized groups? 

wouldn’t you have to actively dismantle certain sets of skills to strengthen others? 

okay great you’ve acquired enough social skills to fit in with white cis straight abled neurotypical people of a certain socioeconomic bracket and you’ve successfully separated yourself from anyone that might taint your status and make you vulnerable to outside devaluation— 

how long can you keep that up? 

how long will it feel like it’s worth it?

title: Far and away, the best accessibility aid is money. It’s money. Money to get the insurance and pay…
content:
Far and away, the best accessibility aid is money. It’s money. Money to get the insurance and pay rent and medical bills and get mobility aids insurance refuses to cover. Ubers to doctor’s appointments, specialist copays, PCP copays, ER bills, ambulance bills, surgery bills, etc etc etc. Disabled people on benefits in America live in enforced poverty. It’s miserable. People are dying from their disabilities solely because they cannot afford the medical care they need.

Being disabled is expensive. So damn fucking expensive.

And it’s utterly infuriating, because it shouldn’t be this costly to stay alive.

title: I’m so tired of performative violence fantasies against abusers derailing conversations that are…
content:
I’m so tired of performative violence fantasies against abusers derailing conversations that are actually materially helping victims. Someone made a great post saying when educating kids about CSA Prevention to never say “I’ll hurt anyone who does this to you” or anything like that because usually it’s someone the kid knows and cares about and they won’t disclose if they think that person will be hurt. Or (which they didn’t mention but I’m adding) in certain types of abuse children are made to believe they are perpetrators when they aren’t and will feel you’ll hurt them and not love them if they disclose. And the comments were just a bunch of stupid, cringey shit about “Well, the kid doesn’t need to know”. Yes, more secrets and gaslighting, that’s what victims need. Shut up. It’s so stupid and not helping the discussion. The kid would find out most likely and would be retraumatized by that. You need to care about victims more than you hate abusers.

Black Fatigue: 

Black Fatigue is a term coined by author

It is 

NOT

 a term for nonblack people to refer to their “fatigue” of Black people.

Gyatt: 

Gyatt, a shortening\quick wording of “Goddamn”, Often to express surprise, disappointment, frustration or disbelief.

It is 

NOT

 a term for ass or butt.

Woke\Stay Woke: 

Woke 

(Or Stay Woke), is a term originating from AAVE used by Black people since the 1930s for staying aware of racism, discrimination and police brutality, and gained political connections in the 70s and further in the 2010’s during 

BLM

 and the 2014 

Ferguson Protests

.

It is 

NOT

 a term for right wingers\conservatives to signal anything diverse as “woke, meaning bad”, It is NOT a joke, to be used sarcastically, ironically, or pejoratively, to be woke is a good thing, it is not negative. title: On this day, 29 August 1997, workers at the Lusty Lady Club in San Francisco voted to join the…
content:
workingclasshistory

:

On this day, 29 August 1997, workers at the Lusty Lady Club in San Francisco voted to join the Exotic Dancers Union, part of a local of the Service Employees International Union (SEIU).

Following a campaign of organising and direct action, which included the women deciding to dance only with their legs closed in protest, they won significant improvements.

Their achievements included guaranteed work shifts, pay increases, removal of one-way mirrors (which enabled clients to film them), and protection from arbitrary discipline and firing. Management also agreed to abolish a racist scheduling practice, under which only one dancer of colour could be on stage at any one time.

The workers later took over the club and ran it as a workers’ co-operative, with elected management.

Three former workers tell their story in our podcast episode 20 about the union: 

https://workingclasshistory.com/2019/03/13/e20-the-exotic-dancers-union/

title: actually there’s no identity you can hold that magically cures you of socialized bigotry. listing…
content:
actually there’s no identity you can hold that magically cures you of socialized bigotry. listing your marginalized identities does not mean you actually did the work to unpack the things you were taught growing up. women need to work to unlearn patriarchy. queer folks need to work to unlearn homophobia. disabled folks need to work to unlearn ablism. POC need to work to unlearn racism. and this is not just “internalized” bigotry - any bigoted ideas you hold toward your own marginalized identity are ideas that you also hold about other people whether you actively engage with those ideas or not.

title: Dutch cops have killed another black man.
content:
Dutch cops have killed another black man.

On 12 September 2026 

Juan Alfredo Goeloe 

and his 7-month pregnant wife were holding a baby shower in Rotterdam when Juan left by bike to retrieve his medication. On his way he was stopped by police who claimed they were looking for a bike thief. He was detained because he did not carry an ID card. Eyewitnesses report that 7 cops sat on top of Juan while he screamed for help, that he was diabetic and that he couldn’t breath. Eventually he stopped moving. He died within walking distance of the baby shower where his wife was waiting for him to cut the cake. 

(source

, 

source

)

Crowd funding for his family: https://www.gofundme.com/f/justice-for-alfredo-jwxjk

This is far from the first time the cops have murdered an innocent, unarmed black man. Black men, immigrants and people with mental disabilities in the Netherlands are far more likely to be murdered by cop than any other demographic. Famous examples of men of color killed by Dutch cops include Mitch Henriquez, Tommy Holten, Sammy Baker, and Jerryson Noor (15 years old). 

See the Ctrl Alt Delete Database: https://overleden.controlealtdelete.nl/

title: The Saddle Lake Cree Nation, located northeast of Edmonton near St. Paul, says health care is a…
content:
The Saddle Lake Cree Nation, located northeast of Edmonton near St. Paul, says health care is a right under Treaty 6 and falls under its inherent jurisdiction. The First Nation has invoked the “medicine chest clause” provision from the treaty signed in 1876, which Indigenous Peoples interpret as a promise to provide comprehensive health care. “All children, including trans and two-spirit children and their family, will have safety under our treaty,” Saddle Lake Chief Dale Steinhauer said on Wednesday.

Hey just so you know… if you’re a legal adult you have the option to just not. You can take that shit off your phone, you don’t have to pick up your phone every time they call, you don’t have to tell them where you’re going all the time, you can just not.

I know it’s scary. I know they will threaten to cut off your phone plan or any financial support they’re giving you or whatever to keep you under their control. But if you can at all manage it… do it. Set a boundary and MEAN it.

At nineteen, I allowed my mom to cut off my phone plan because she would SCREAM at me over the phone until I was sobbing because I didn’t call her often enough (…turns out I have ADHD and time blindness but we didn’t know that then). At a certain point I just turned to my partner and asked if we could survive without my mom paying for our phone plan, and we could, and I didn’t speak to my mother again for 15 years or so. And my life is better for that.
